summary: Admit Ozon Pay as a separate finance surface with encrypted Seller API credentials and a bounded prerequisite health probe; merchant payment operations remain qualification-gated.

impacts.evidence: Ozon Pay credentials are bound to one tenant-scoped connector account; no caller-supplied tenant override is accepted.
Client IDs and API keys stay behind SecretProvider; payment credentials and Seller API bodies are not persisted or logged.
No public HTTP/OpenAPI operation is added; the existing connector-account control plane is reused.
No event or canonical envelope is added.
The adapter uses Connector SDK v1 and declares payment capabilities in the manifest while runtime admission keeps them closed.
No provider-specific table or migration is introduced.
The host performs a fixed TLS-verified Seller API probe and receives credential bytes only inside the callback-scoped secret path.
Payment creation, refund and webhook processing are not admitted; future writes require payment policy and merchant qualification.
Health checks reuse connector.account.connection_checked with safe status metadata only.
No remote payment write or retry path is enabled; future admission must qualify idempotent merchant operations.
Only a fixed outbound Seller API probe is added; no payment webhook ingress or unsigned callback is accepted.
Manifest timeout/retry metadata and normalized provider-unavailable health states bound the probe.
The finance entry can be disabled through runtime support without a migration or destructive rollback.
Deterministic connector and host transport tests cover credential shape, callback use and bounded request routing; the machine report records SDK checks.
